## Withdrawn

| edge | was | why |
|---|---|---|
| GR-0096 | relevant market — *related* → deceased person | The sentence states what the relevant market must know of a deceased person's name; the relation it bears on is the section 43 ground, which other records state, not one between the market and the person. |
| GR-0107 | examiner — *related* → specification of goods and services | The examiner suggests that the applicant restrict the specification; the act is the applicant's limitation, and an examiner-to-specification link would say nothing of it. |
| GR-0108 | endorsement — *related* → specification of goods and services | A drafting instruction on what an endorsement mentions; no relation between the endorsement and the specification as such. |
| GR-0123 | geographical reference — *related* → ordinary consumer | The criteria run through the consumer's association and confusion; geographical reference qualifies the test (GR-0079) and the ordinary consumer qualifies confusion (GR-0101) already. |
| GR-0144 | connotation — *related* → top level domain | The sentence is about how the application is considered; the top level domain's bearing on the section 43 ground is GR-0148. |
| GR-0162 | evidence of use — *related* → other circumstances | Evidence and other circumstances are two alternative ways past a section 41 ground; neither relates to the other. |
| GR-0173 | decision maker — *related* → descriptive matter | The tolerance of some confusion where a trader built a business on a descriptive term is descriptive matter qualifying confusion (GR-0180); the decision maker adds nothing. |
| GR-0174 | decision maker — *related* → deception | That the decision maker must be clearly satisfied is a standard every test shares; a link from the role to deception says nothing a reader can use. |
| GR-0224 | substantially identical — *related* → closely related goods and services | Substantial identity and closely related goods are two separate limbs of section 44; the sentence relates each to the section, not to each other. |
| GR-0225 | substantially identical — *related* → surrounding circumstances | About a similar mark's use as a circumstance under section 41(4); no relation between the section 44 test and surrounding circumstances. |
| GR-0227 | substantially identical — *related* → registered trade mark | A section 102 comparison names both; the test is not about registered trade marks as such. |
| GR-0228 | substantially identical — *related* → similarity of goods and services | Two separate limbs of section 44 (the marks, the goods); neither relates to the other. |
| GR-0230 | other circumstances — *related* → deferment of acceptance | Deferment is granted to gather evidence of other circumstances; neither causes, requires nor qualifies the other. |
| GR-0236 | sign — *related* → denotation | The question is whether use has displaced a sign's primary meaning; a sign-to-denotation link restates it without the use that does the work. |
| GR-0246 | use of a trade mark — *related* → removal for non-use | About costs and a certificate of use in a non-use opposition; use preventing removal is stated from a passage that says so (new edge below). |
| GR-0251 | transmission — *related* → written permission | The consent meant is the ACCC's, not a well-known person's written permission, which is what GC-0029 is. |
| GR-0257 | deferment of acceptance — *related* → prior use | Deferment is granted to gather evidence of prior use; neither causes, requires nor qualifies the other. |
| GR-0258 | deferment of acceptance — *related* → honest concurrent use | Deferment is granted to gather evidence of honest concurrent use; neither causes, requires nor qualifies the other. |
| GR-0265 | endorsement — *related* → specification of goods and services | An endorsement and a limitation are alternative remedies; GR-0697 and GR-0698 state what each does. |
| GR-0279 | Madrid Protocol — *related* → international registration designating Australia | The sentence is about extensions of time, which the Protocol does not provide; that the Protocol governs IRDAs is GR-0282. |
| GR-0280 | Madrid Protocol — *related* → examination | About refusal notices during the 18-month period; no relation between the Protocol and examination as such. |
| GR-0303 | classification of goods and services — *related* → examiner | About where an examiner looks up classification; the specification's dependence on the classification is GR-0301. |
| GR-0304 | amendment of an application — *related* → classification of goods and services | The classification corrected is the application's own, not the classification system the concept names. |
| GR-0316 | filing date — *related* → pending application | A rule refusing deferment where a cited pending application has the same filing date; no relation between the date and pending applications as such. |
| GR-0317 | date of registration — *related* → Convention country | The date is that of the application made in the Convention country; the country itself is incidental. |
| GR-0324 | extension of time — *related* → statement of grounds and particulars | The sentence is about the form of an extension request; the approved form is GR-0336. |
| GR-0327 | deceptively similar — *related* → similarity of goods and services | About the scope of a registration's protection; the two tests are separate limbs of section 44 and the sentence relates neither to the other. |
| GR-0331 | deceptively similar — *related* → closely related goods and services | Deceptive similarity and closely related goods are separate limbs of section 44. |
| GR-0341 | divisional application — *related* → Convention country | About the priority date of a divisional application; the Convention country is incidental. |
| GR-0349 | registration number — *related* → Office of origin | The IB advising the Office of origin of a number; the sentence names the IB only as "IB", which recognition does not take, and the Office of origin is incidental. |
| GR-0369 | holder of an international registration — *related* → Record of International Registrations | The holder may seek rectification; the Record itself is incidental. |
| GR-0397 | ground for rejection — *related* → trade mark application | A worked example of a section 42(b) ground; the application is incidental. |
| GR-0398 | presumption of registrability — *related* → Registrar | The presumption's displacement once the Registrar is satisfied is what GR-0091 and GR-0092 state (constrains the Registrar). |
| GR-0401 | reputation — *related* → ordinary consumer | A place's reputation influencing consumers is reputation qualifying confusion (GR-0474). |
| GR-0402 | surrounding circumstances — *related* → deceased person | A case's circumstances (Princess Diana's fame); an example, not a relation. |
| GR-0405 | endorsement — *related* → well-known person | The endorsement names the well-known person who consented; what the endorsement records is the written permission (GR-0435). |
| GR-0411 | geographical indication — *related* → originate | A cross-reference to the definition of "originate"; no relation stated. |
| GR-0416 | INN stem — *related* → pharmaceutical or veterinary substance | That an INN stem names a family of substances is a definition, not a relation between the two concepts. |
| GR-0426 | well-known person — *related* → written permission | The written permission overcomes the section 43 ground (GR-0687); the person-to-permission link adds nothing. |
| GR-0428 | transmission — *related* → deceased person | The deceased person here is a deceased owner whose mark devolves; GC-0027 is a deceased person a mark refers to. |
| GR-0438 | phoneword — *related* → connotation | "Secondary meaning" here is acquired distinctiveness under section 41, not the section 43 connotation GC-0001 names. |
| GR-0441 | top level domain — *related* → trade mark application | About considering the application as a whole; no relation between the domain and the application. |
| GR-0442 | radio call sign — *related* → registered owner | The sentence says confusion arises if the owner does not hold the call sign's licence — a condition, not a fact that the owner holds it. |
| GR-0455 | revocation of acceptance — *related* → Contracting Party of the holder | The sentence names the Office of the Contracting Party of the holder, which GC-0149 then excluded; incidental to revocation in any case. |
| GR-0476 | examiner research — *related* → image of a person | Research supporting a section 42 ground; the image of a person is incidental. |
| GR-0486 | ordinary signification — *related* → similarity of goods and services | The two-step test is ordinary signification and other traders' legitimate desire (GR-0213, GR-0214); similar goods are part of the second step. |
| GR-0492 | honest concurrent use — *related* → revocation of registration | A long comparison of procedures; no relation stated between honest concurrent use and revocation. |
| GR-0510 | authorised user — *related* → predecessor in title | A list of whose use counts; no relation between the authorised user and the predecessor. |
| GR-0516 | transmission — *related* → Commission | The sentence says no consent of the Commission is needed for a transmission; a negative the dictionary cannot state, and assignment's need for consent is GR-0432. |
| GR-0519 | authorised user — *related* → registered trade mark | Who may sue for infringement; the ontology holds no infringement concept to state it with. |
| GR-0523 | priority date — *related* → international registration of a trade mark | A condition on claiming priority for a subsequent designation; too conditional to state as a relation of the two concepts. |
| GR-0533 | deferment of acceptance — *related* → prescribed court | Acceptance is deferred while an appeal is possible; the court is incidental. |
| GR-0535 | lapsing of an application — *related* → divisional application | About a cited application that has lapsed; the divisional application is incidental. |
| GR-0540 | evidence of use — *related* → predecessor in title | A list of whose use the evidence may show; no relation between the evidence and the predecessor as such. |
| GR-0544 | opposition — *related* → ART | Review of the Registrar's decisions by the ART is GR-0569. |
| GR-0546 | notice of opposition — *related* → international registration designating Australia | That an IRDA can be opposed is GR-0283; the notice is incidental. |
| GR-0550 | opposition — *related* → removal for non-use | About costs; that a non-use application can be opposed is GR-0604. |
| GR-0553 | renewal of registration — *related* → Office of origin | When renewal of an international registration falls due; the Office of origin is incidental. |
| GR-0554 | certification trade mark — *related* → Commission | The Commission's consent to assigning a certification trade mark is GR-0432. |
| GR-0560 | holder of an international registration — *related* → Madrid Protocol | The country through which a holder applies; no relation stated between the holder and the Protocol. |
| GR-0561 | Madrid Protocol — *related* → International Bureau | A heading of the Protocol's regulations; no relation stated. |
| GR-0562 | Office of origin — *related* → Madrid Protocol | An explanation of a form field; no relation stated. |
| GR-0567 | protected international trade mark — *related* → Office of origin | About transformation after the basic mark ceases in the Office of origin; no relation between the mark and the Office as such. |
| GR-0570 | opponent — *related* → application for removal | An opponent is a party to the opposition (GR-0294); referral of the non-use application is incidental. |
| GR-0578 | classification of goods and services — *related* → Office of origin | The International Bureau's opinion prevailing over the Office of origin is GR-0601. |
| GR-0583 | plant variety name — *related* → examination | A word's special meaning in plant examination; no relation stated. |
| GR-0585 | Registrar's decision — *related* → ART | Review of the Registrar's decisions by the ART is GR-0569. |
| GR-0592 | holder of an international registration — *related* → extension of protection | About replacement of a national registration; no relation between the holder and extension of protection as such. |
| GR-0595 | ART — *related* → certification trade mark | The ART's review of the Commission's decisions is GR-0594. |
| GR-0599 | Office of origin — *related* → international registration of a trade mark | About certification by the Office of origin and when the IB must receive the application; too procedural to state as a relation of the two concepts. |
| GR-0600 | holder of an international registration — *related* → Office of origin | A consequence of an Office's state leaving the Protocol; no relation between the holder and the Office as such. |
| GR-0606 | notice of opposition — *related* → extension of protection | That extension of protection can be opposed is GR-0450; the notice is incidental. |
| GR-0612 | Contracting Party of the holder — *related* → holder of an international registration | The sentence names the Office of the Contracting Party of the holder, which GC-0149 excluded; the link was not about the concept it named. |
| GR-0613 | Contracting Party of the holder — *related* → international registration designating Australia | As GR-0612. |
| GR-0626 | notice of intention to defend — *related* → extension of protection | A consequence of not filing a notice of intention to defend; the opposition's outcome, not a relation of the notice and extension of protection. |
| GR-0629 | application for removal — *related* → notice of intention to defend | That the notice of intention to defend follows the notice of opposition is GR-0319. |
| GR-0630 | pending application — *related* → repealed Act | A heading (section 240); no relation stated. |
| GR-0098 | ordinary consumer — *qualifies* → scent trade mark | The "ordinary person searching the Register" who must understand a scent mark's representation, not the ordinary consumer of the deception and confusion tests. |
| GR-0168 | surrounding circumstances — *qualifies* → revocation of acceptance | "All the relevant circumstances" of a revocation, not the surrounding circumstances of the deception and confusion tests. |
| GR-0226 | substantially identical — *qualifies* → evidence of use | Evidence of use may be of a substantially identical mark; a rule about what evidence counts, which no predicate states between the test and the evidence. |
| GR-0293 | withdrawal — *allocatesTo* → Registrar | The Registrar publishes a withdrawal the applicant makes; "performs" would say the Registrar withdraws. |
| GR-0427 | reputation — *qualifies* → deceased person | The person's fame and how recently they died bear on consumers' expectations under the section 43 ground, not on the deceased person as such. |
| GR-0493 | predecessor in title — *qualifies* → prior use | The rule is that a person relying on a predecessor's prior use must be the assignee of its goodwill; the ontology holds no goodwill concept to state it with. |
| GR-0525 | filing date — *qualifies* → convention application | The date at which a priority claim's criteria must hold; no relation the dictionary can state between the date and the application. |
| GR-0556 | reputation — *qualifies* → defensive trade mark | The reputation meant is the trade mark's own, which is GR-0555 (GC-0130); GC-0050 is the reputation of a place or person (ruling A3). |

## New

| edge | relationship | why |
|---|---|---|
| GR-0703 | geographical qualifier — *qualifies* → geographical reference | Qualifying information ("made in", "product of") changes what a geographical reference claims, and so how it is assessed. |
| GR-0704 | wine geographical indication — *isProtectedThrough* → Register of Protected Geographical Indications and Other Terms | Wine geographical indications are protected by entry on the Wine Register (ruling A4). |
| GR-0705 | term protected under the Wine Australia Act — *isProtectedThrough* → Register of Protected Geographical Indications and Other Terms | A term is protected under the Wine Australia Act once it is on the Wine Register, and not before. |
| GR-0706 | IP Australia — *performs* → examination | Examination is IP Australia's process, as the office in which the Registrar's functions are exercised. |
| GR-0707 | capable of distinguishing — *appliesTo* → services of a person | The test asks whether the mark distinguishes the applicant's services from the services of other persons, the term section 6 defines. |
| GR-0708 | office practice — *appliesTo* → acceptance | Office practice governs when acceptance is published. |
| GR-0709 | Registrar — *actsAs* → Contracting Party of the holder | For a request made through the Trade Marks Office, the Registrar performs that Office's functions. |
| GR-0710 | top level domain — *isPartOf* → internet domain name | A top level domain is the last segment of a domain name — a part of it, not a kind of it. |
| GR-0711 | International Bureau — *keeps* → International Register | The International Bureau maintains the International Register. |
| GR-0712 | Registrar — *keeps* → Record of International Registrations | The Registrar maintains the Record of International Registrations (reg 17A.66). |
| GR-0713 | Registrar — *keeps* → Register of Trade Marks | The Register is kept at the Trade Marks Office, and the Registrar makes its entries (s 207). |
| GR-0714 | IP Australia — *actsAs* → Office of origin | For an international application filed from Australia, IP Australia is the Office of origin and certifies the application. |

## Re-typed

| concept | kind | why |
|---|---|---|
| presumption of registrability | principle | The presumption of registrability is a rule about how the grounds are applied — accept unless satisfied a ground exists (s 33(1)) — neither a ground nor a test; none_of_these said only that no kind fitted it. |
| mandatory application of the section | principle | That section 43 applies mandatorily is a rule about the decision maker's discretion, not a question to answer. |
| office practice | principle | Office practice is how the office applies the Act where it leaves room — the Manual's own standing, practice rather than law. |
| date of registration | context | A date, as the filing date and the priority date are; the context kind already holds dates. |
| pending application | instrument or record | A pending application is a trade mark application in a status (s 11), and applications are instruments or records. |
| repealed Act | external instrument | The repealed Act (the 1955 Act) is a statute other than the 1995 Act that practice still refers to; the kind now holds statutes as well as treaties. |
| owner or authorised user | process role | The concept names a person — the owner, registrant or licensed operator of a phoneword, domain name or call sign — not a circumstance. |
| international registration of a trade mark | subject matter | An international registration is a registration, as a registered trade mark is, and an IRDA is a kind of one; its entry on the International Register is a relationship (isRecordedIn). |
| originate | context | Where wine originates — tied by section 15 to where its grapes were grown — is a fact about the goods the assessment looks at, not a question the decision maker answers. |

## Signed links corrected

| correction | concept | withdrawn | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| GK-0030 | connotation | narrower decision maker | The signed record says the decision maker is a kind of connotation; it is a role, connotation a test. Nothing in the corpus relates them hierarchically. |
| GK-0031 | geographical reference | narrower geographical origin | Geographical origin (where the goods come from) is not a kind of geographical reference (a thing in the mark), and GC-0019's own not-label is "geographical reference". A geographical reference indicates a geographical origin (GR-0410). |
| GK-0032 | geographical origin | broader geographical reference | As the correction of GC-0017 — the other end of the same link. |
| GK-0033 | internet domain name | narrower top level domain | A top level domain is a part of a domain name, not a kind of one. |
| GK-0034 | top level domain | broader internet domain name | As the correction of GC-0032 — the other end of the same link. |
| GK-0035 | relevant market | narrower ordinary consumer | The ordinary consumer is a member of the relevant market, not a kind of market. No sentence names both, so no "part of" link replaces it; both qualify the same tests (GR-0067, GR-0080). |
| GK-0036 | ordinary consumer | broader relevant market | As the correction of GC-0009 — the other end of the same link. |
